n-php2shell.title: PHP2Shell coins
n-php2shell.summary: Coins named for PHP2Shell, the name security posts give to two critical PHP core flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 9.2 each, unauthenticated remote code execution). Posts of 2026-10-21 (e1:8) say the PHP project would ship an emergency security release at 14:00 UTC that day; at 15:35 UTC Rapid7 posted that the PHP project had announced security releases for the two flaws and that exploitation in the wild was expected, and a security-news account linked a Register article headlined that PHP developers published the fix and warned site owners to pull unpatched servers offline (e1:8). A post of 2026-10-22 summarising an AWS report says exploitation was seen on 2026-10-17, four days before disclosure (e1:8; not verified here). Four pump.fun coins carry the story in their own metadata: PHP-UP-2026 (PHP), whose description reads "They dropped an exploit that allows you to drain money from anyone." and whose pool was created at 05:14 UTC on 2026-10-21, before the 14:00 UTC release; two coins named PHP2SHELL (pools created at 04:21 UTC and 21:30 UTC on 2026-10-21, empty descriptions); and Saviour of the Internet (SURY), created at 00:05 UTC on 2026-10-22, whose description says its fees go to Ondrej Sury's GitHub (@oerdj) and credits him with rushing out emergency PHP patches. Posts of 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22 (e2:0) say a Debian PHP package maintainer named Sury published patched packages, including backports to end-of-life PHP versions, and one repeats the claim that the coin's fees go to his GitHub. The fee routing and any payout are the coin's own claim and are not verified, and no coin is shown to be affiliated with the PHP project, the researchers who found the flaws or Sury.
